results.content: Add Paper to My Library. Using these links will ensure access to this page indefinitely. 52 Pages Posted: 8 Jul 2025. This study addresses this gap by assessing the accessibility of shelters in Barcelona using a mobility justice framework. We ask: How do the spatial distribution of shelters and socio-economic conditions contribute to inequalities in access for vulnerable populations? We aim to (1) assess the spatial and temporal accessibility of shelters within a 10-minute walk, using a reduced walking speed (3.28 km/h); and (2) analyse the socio-economic profiles of neighbourhoods with and without access. Using GIS-based isochrone analysis and demographic data, we map access to shelter for adults aged 65+ and children aged 3-4, while also examining intersectional vulnerabilities, including income level and migrant background. Accessibility gaps are most pronounced in low-income and migrant-dense areas. **Keywords:** Urban proximity, Equitable accessibility, Climate adaptation, Climate shelters, Mobility justice, Social Inclusion.
